question: An engineer configures a Messages API request with two entries in mcp_servers, 'billing-mcp' and 'support-mcp', but only adds one MCPToolset in the tools array, referencing 'billing-mcp'. What happens?
options: A) The request succeeds, and support-mcp is silently ignored while only billing-mcp tools remain callable.
B) The request succeeds, and Claude automatically falls back to using all tools from support-mcp with system default settings.
C) The API merges both servers into a single implicit toolset and enables every tool from both servers by default.
D) The API returns a validation error because every server defined in mcp_servers must be referenced by exactly one MCPToolset.
correct_answers: D) The API returns a validation error because every server defined in mcp_servers must be referenced by exactly one MCPToolset.
explanations: Incorrect. The request is rejected at validation time rather than silently proceeding with a subset of servers.
Incorrect. There is no automatic fallback that grants an unreferenced server's tools system-default access.
Incorrect. The API does not merge servers into an implicit toolset; each server needs its own explicit MCPToolset entry.
Correct. Validation requires every server listed in mcp_servers to be referenced by exactly one MCPToolset; an unreferenced server triggers a validation error.
